To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the colostral volume, protein concentration and cell and macro-phage counts were significantly lower in preterm compared to fullterm colostrum, but sIgA concentration was higher.
the colostral cells and anti-micriobial proteins are significantly different between pre-term and full-term colostra.
the concentration and cell count in the colostral samples of mothers delivering preterm were significantly higher than those of mothers delivering full-term babies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of gestational age on the volume, concentration, and cellular constituents of colostrums.
the composition of colostrums of mothers delivering preterm and term babies.
the immunological factors of human colostrum and milk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the colostral cells and anti-microbials are not only important in providing the initial protection to the newborn but also in maintaining the health and well being of the pre-term infant.
colostrum is an excellent source of anti-infective and anti-oxidative agents.
the colostral factors, both anti-infective and cellular, are significantly influenced by the gestational age and degree of prematurity of the baby.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pre-term colostrums are rich in protective factors and are thus a good source of nutrition and immunity in the pre-term infants.
colostrum is the first milk produced by the mammary gland of the mother after the birth.
colostrum is a complex mixture of immunoglobulin, enzymes and other proteins, which are secreted by different types of cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colostrum is a very rich source of immunoglobulins, lactoferrin and other proteins, and cells.
the colostral cells and proteins are influenced by the gestational age of the baby.
the mothers delivering pre-term infants should be encouraged to breastfeed as early as possible and to breastfeed exclusively for at least 6 months.
